# Positions — Product

Recurring stances across the roster. Each is a paraphrase; the links open the video at the moment the case is made.

## Discovery and user research

### 1. Don't implement a customer's literal request; treat repeated complaints as clues to a shared underlying pain rather than a spec to build.
- Jason Cohen — [The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)](https://youtu.be/8xLquwfx6p0?t=1978)

### 2. Even without a large customer base, directly talking to people who are struggling or leaving gives usable signal cheaply.
- Jason Cohen — [The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)](https://youtu.be/8xLquwfx6p0?t=2008)

### 3. Leaders should personally stay hands-on with the product/customers so their intuition stays accurate instead of trusting secondhand reports or slides.
- Keith Rabois — [Hard truths about building in the AI era | Keith Rabois (Khosla Ventures)](https://youtu.be/xCd9ykretlg?t=2609)

### 4. Correlational signals about 'what good customers share' are only useful once compared against what struggling customers also share, isolating the actual difference.
- Jason Cohen — [The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)](https://youtu.be/8xLquwfx6p0?t=2036)

## Roadmap and prioritization

### 5. As AI makes execution cheap, the scarce and valuable skill becomes exercising judgment about which ideas to greenlight and fund, not doing the work itself.
- Jessica Fain — [The art of influence: The single most important skill left that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain](https://youtu.be/RP4vJeIb7WU?t=4286)
- The Skip Podcast — [How Meta Is Reinventing Product Management](https://youtu.be/5y3kx8TTsaI?t=23)
- Geoff Charles — [Inside Ramp, the $32B Company Where AI Agents Run Everything | Geoff Charles](https://youtu.be/RBqT2PHWdBg?t=1880)
- Jenny Wen — [The design process is dead. Here’s what’s replacing it. | Jenny Wen (head of design at Claude)](https://youtu.be/eh8bcBIAAFo?t=1710)
- Andrew Ambrosino — [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](https://youtu.be/P3KDebPTUrw?t=611)

### 6. Sustainable growth comes from ruthlessly saying no to most feature ideas and distractions, keeping a narrow, clear focus on the core product goal.
- Jean Lee — [Building WhatsApp with Jean Lee](https://youtu.be/5Kn32cIWPSY?t=3893)

### 7. Avoid committing to long, detailed roadmaps; keep only near-term visibility (weeks to a month) so you stay free to follow new discoveries as they emerge.
- 37signals — [Don't Write It Down – REWORK](https://youtu.be/Rz9nGlbRmko?t=551)

### 8. Before building something new or 'better,' first master everything already proven in the category so you've earned the right to change it.
- Mark Pincus — [The Hidden Pattern Behind Winning Products | Farmville creator Mark Pincus](https://youtu.be/iGx8RDvMvsg?t=1661)

### 9. Ship imperfect or early versions fast, labeled honestly, then iterate quickly on real feedback rather than waiting to build the 'right' product first.

# Disagreements — Product

Live debates where the roster pulls in different directions. One link per side, at the moment the case is made.

## Discovery and user research

### 1. How much weight should a single customer's specific ask get versus only acting on patterns seen across many customers?
- **Ignore any one customer's literal fix suggestion; only patterns repeated across the whole base justify a change.**
  - 37signals — [Don't Write It Down – REWORK](https://youtu.be/Rz9nGlbRmko?t=26)
- **Individual conversations with at-risk or struggling customers are directly worth acting on, even at small scale.**
  - Jason Cohen — [The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)](https://youtu.be/8xLquwfx6p0?t=2003)

### 2. Should you launch only once you already have conviction it will succeed, or is launching an admittedly unfinished version to gather real signal still correct?
- **Don't launch on hope; the best builders already know their release is a hit before shipping it.**
  - Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=2074)
- **Ship a minimal version deliberately, accepting it lacks many features, because real usage teaches things internal debate can't.**
  - Mike Krieger — [How to Build an Agent-native Product | Mike Krieger](https://youtu.be/KRv9GpJYrUA?t=647)

## Roadmap and prioritization

### 3. Should teams commit to and communicate a detailed forward-looking roadmap?
- **No — keep the roadmap undefined and short-horizon; work is discovered iteratively and long-range planning wastes energy and blocks new opportunities.**
  - 37signals — [Don't Write It Down – REWORK](https://youtu.be/Rz9nGlbRmko?t=551)
- **Yes — written planning docs are valuable for getting large stakeholder groups (legal, safety, exec) rowing in the same direction, especially on ambiguous new bets.**
  - Dianne Penn — [How Anthropic builds products like Claude Code before the AI models are ready | Dianne Penn](https://youtu.be/tivaWTTVRhY?t=2891)

### 4. Should product managers still write traditional, detailed requirement docs before building?
- **Detailed PRDs are being replaced by a one-paragraph problem statement plus a prototype and, for ML-heavy work, an eval set.**
  - The Skip Podcast — [How Meta Is Reinventing Product Management](https://youtu.be/5y3kx8TTsaI?t=324)
- **Full PRDs remain valuable, particularly for exploring ambiguous opportunities where the technology isn't ready for every user yet.**
  - Dianne Penn — [How Anthropic builds products like Claude Code before the AI models are ready | Dianne Penn](https://youtu.be/tivaWTTVRhY?t=2949)

## Shipping and working with engineering

### 5. Can AI-written code be safely auto-approved without human review, or is AI code quality trending down, requiring more caution?
- **With a proper scoring harness, automated AI review/approval can be faster and safer than human-reviewed PRs.**
  - How I AI Podcast — [I built an AI code review bot in 30 minutes - here’s how](https://youtu.be/cmATJGbA8bI?t=252)
- **Industry-wide, AI-generated code quality is visibly worsening, so teams should slow down and verify more.**
  - Pragmatic Engineer — [Building Pi, and what makes self-modifying software so fascinating](https://youtu.be/n5f51gtuGHE?t=31)

### 6. Should PMs still write formal specs (now aimed at AI agents) or skip specs and build/prototype directly?
- **Specs remain necessary, just rewritten as agent-readable prompts rather than engineer-facing docs.**
  - Geoff Charles — [Inside Ramp, the $32B Company Where AI Agents Run Everything | Geoff Charles](https://youtu.be/RBqT2PHWdBg?t=138)
- **Skip specs; a working prototype convinces stakeholders faster than any written doc or design.**
  - Peter Yang — [Give Me 20 Minutes, I'll Make You AI Native](https://youtu.be/vCwTc39Otm8?t=437)

## Metrics, growth and experimentation

### 7. Should teams ship and test continuously, or hold back until near-certain of quality?
- **Push work out fast and iterate via continuous small experiments and rollouts.**
  - Lenny's Podcast — [How Anthropic is using Claude to automate its own growth (and why old playbooks are obsolete)](https://youtu.be/k-H4nsOTuxU?t=2193)
- **Withhold shipping until internal testing gives near-certainty, avoiding premature live experiments.**
  - Jean Lee — [Building WhatsApp with Jean Lee](https://youtu.be/5Kn32cIWPSY?t=1471)

### 8. Can AI agents run the growth-experimentation loop end-to-end, or does human judgment stay essential?
- **AI tooling can now identify, build, test and ship growth experiments with minimal human effort.**
  - Lenny's Podcast — [How Anthropic is using Claude to automate its own growth (and why old playbooks are obsolete)](https://youtu.be/k-H4nsOTuxU?t=2238)
- **Cross-functional alignment and influence remain a non-automatable human skill in running experiments and product decisions.**
  - Lenny's Podcast — [How Anthropic is using Claude to automate its own growth (and why old playbooks are obsolete)](https://youtu.be/k-H4nsOTuxU?t=2244)
  - Jessica Fain — [The art of influence: The single most important skill left that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain](https://youtu.be/RP4vJeIb7WU?t=4322)

## The product role and craft

### 9. Are classic PM skills like stakeholder management, prioritization, and frameworks now obsolete because code is cheap?
- **These skills are outdated relics of a pre-AI era and no longer the point of the job.**
  - Geoff Charles — [Inside Ramp, the $32B Company Where AI Agents Run Everything | Geoff Charles](https://youtu.be/RBqT2PHWdBg?t=1759)
- **Cross-functional alignment and influence are still essential and are not going away anytime soon.**
  - Lenny's Podcast — [How Anthropic is using Claude to automate its own growth (and why old playbooks are obsolete)](https://youtu.be/k-H4nsOTuxU?t=2244)
  - Jessica Fain — [The art of influence: The single most important skill left that AI can’t replace | Jessica Fain](https://youtu.be/RP4vJeIb7WU?t=92)

### 10. Will AI eventually be able to fully replicate human taste and judgment, or does that stay a human domain?
- **AI's sense of taste and judgment is improving fast and may be undervalued in how good it will get.**
  - Jenny Wen — [The design process is dead. Here’s what’s replacing it. | Jenny Wen (head of design at Claude)](https://youtu.be/eh8bcBIAAFo?t=1710)
- **AI still cannot replace real marketing or product judgment and taste, especially for distinctive copy and positioning.**
  - The Next Wave — [I Let Claude Replace My Marketing Team. Here’s What Happened](https://youtu.be/-PFKQKZ3YB8?t=126)

# Frameworks & vocabulary — Product

Named models, rules of thumb and terms of art the roster uses.

## Discovery and user research

### MVP vs Maximum Launchable Product
A distinction between shipping a bare 'viable' product to hope-test the market versus launching only once you believe it's already a hit.
- Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=2092)

### Don't Write It Down
Rule that individual customer feature requests shouldn't be logged and tracked; only recurring themes across many anecdotes should drive roadmap decisions.
- 37signals — [Don't Write It Down – REWORK](https://youtu.be/Rz9nGlbRmko?t=333)

### Adapted Five W's for churn
A root-cause questioning technique used to push past a customer's stated cancellation reason (e.g. price) to the real underlying driver.
- Jason Cohen — [The surprising advice from a founder who built 2 unicorns | Jason Cohen (WP Engine)](https://youtu.be/8xLquwfx6p0?t=1974)

## Roadmap and prioritization

### PRD (product requirements doc) as alignment vehicle
A written doc used not to specify code but to align a large cross-functional group on the problem, goals, and source of truth before building.
- Dianne Penn — [How Anthropic builds products like Claude Code before the AI models are ready | Dianne Penn](https://youtu.be/tivaWTTVRhY?t=2891)
- The Skip Podcast — [How Meta Is Reinventing Product Management](https://youtu.be/5y3kx8TTsaI?t=324)

### "All new fails" mantra
A guiding rule that any new feature should be assumed to fail, so you test many small variants of many ideas instead of betting on one.
- Mark Pincus — [The Hidden Pattern Behind Winning Products | Farmville creator Mark Pincus](https://youtu.be/iGx8RDvMvsg?t=1604)

### Proven-vs-new deconstruction
Before greenlighting a new feature, require the team to prove deep mastery of every existing best-in-class example in that category.
- Mark Pincus — [The Hidden Pattern Behind Winning Products | Farmville creator Mark Pincus](https://youtu.be/iGx8RDvMvsg?t=1682)

## Shipping and working with engineering

### Kill hope before hope kills you
A rule of thumb distinguishing belief (grounded in data) from hope, used to force teams to cut unproven bets quickly.
- Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=2001)

### Progressive delivery / canary deployment
A named evolution beyond continuous delivery: roll changes out to a subset of traffic first, observe, then ramp up gradually.
- Robert Erez — [CI/CD with Robert Erez](https://youtu.be/2x0eq5oDOJY?t=2398)

## Metrics, growth and experimentation

### Proven, Better, New
Evaluate new product ideas by starting from what's proven in market, making it clearly better, then adding one new wrinkle.
- Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=620)

### ASN (Active Social Network)
A proprietary metric counting reciprocal social round-trips between users, used to predict and drive return visits.
- Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=2795)

### Sinking speedboat
Metaphor for high-virality, low-retention products that must fix the underlying leak rather than just adding more users.
- Mark Pincus — [The Hidden Pattern Behind Winning Products | Farmville creator Mark Pincus](https://youtu.be/iGx8RDvMvsg?t=1278)

### Bold beat
Adding a whole new dimension (e.g., social, identity) to a stale product category to reinvigorate engagement.
- Mark Pincus — [The hidden pattern behind successful products | Mark Pincus (FarmVille, Words with Friends, & more)](https://youtu.be/7eh9C3TUotc?t=2549)

### Max MRR
A ceiling on monthly recurring revenue implied by churn versus acquisition rate, used to judge sustainability of growth.
- Tibo Louis-Lucas — [How This Solo AI Founder Bootstrapped 5 Products to 1M+ / Month | Tibo Louis-Lucas](https://youtu.be/0UnZnonMN9o?t=2295)

## The product role and craft

### First principles thinking
A named evaluation lens PMs use to reason from incentives and fundamentals rather than pattern-matching past playbooks.
- The Skip Podcast — [How Meta Is Reinventing Product Management](https://youtu.be/5y3kx8TTsaI?t=3027)
- Dianne Penn — [How Anthropic builds products like Claude Code before the AI models are ready | Dianne Penn](https://youtu.be/tivaWTTVRhY?t=2432)

### Product leader as curator
Named idea that the best product leaders succeed by curating people, ideas, and strategy rather than generating everything themselves.
- Adam Mosseri — [The rise of taste, human authenticity and judgment in an AI world | Adam Mosseri (Head of IG)](https://youtu.be/yQ_EWmtfWvQ?t=1878)

### Evals are the new PRDs
A named reframing where writing evaluation sets, not PRDs, is how research PMs express product judgment and user value.
- Dianne Penn — [How Anthropic builds products like Claude Code before the AI models are ready | Dianne Penn](https://youtu.be/tivaWTTVRhY?t=60)

### Zones (genius/curiosity/competence)
A personal framework for mapping which work energizes you versus drains you, used to decide what to keep doing.
- Peter Yang — [I Quit My High Paying Product Job to Bet on Myself](https://youtu.be/T4pvKvAE_SA?t=226)

### Two-week rule for engineer-as-PM
A named threshold: if a project takes under two engineering weeks, the engineer is expected to act as its PM.
- Lenny's Podcast — [How Anthropic is using Claude to automate its own growth (and why old playbooks are obsolete)](https://youtu.be/k-H4nsOTuxU?t=2736)
